conventions.convention: Generator rows have nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero row sum; discount c is strictly positive. The Bellman equation is cV_i=max_a(Q_i^a V+r_i^a).
Howard iteration switches only on strict improvement, retains tied current actions, chooses the least-index maximizing replacement, and distinguishes convergence from budget exhaustion.
The torus has unit periods, h_j=1/N_j with N_j≥3, and every coordinate index wraps modulo N_j. Interpolation uses nonnegative tensor-product corner weights.

The first-order Hamiltonian is H=max_a(-b_a·p−ℓ_a), so u_t=min_a(b_a·Du+ℓ_a). Numerical updates take minima and use the foot x+τb_a; compact-control errors must vanish uniformly on every bounded momentum set.
The second-order equation is u_t−max_a{Σ_j(α_j^a u_xjxj+b_j^a u_xj)+f^a}=0, with finite controls, jointly Lipschitz coefficients and α_j^a≥α_*>0.
The diffusion stencil uses backward drift differences for b≥0 and forward differences for b<0. Admission requires both |b_j^a|h_j≤α_j^a and τ max_i,a Σ_j(2α_j^a/h_j²+|b_j^a|/h_j)≤1.
Closed elliptic jets require convergence of base points, function values, gradients and matrices. Space-time elliptic jets include the full time and mixed Hessian entries.

USC subsolutions are tested from above at local maxima with residual ≤0; LSC supersolutions are tested from below with residual ≥0. Second-order tests are C^{1,2}, and initial conditions use joint relaxed traces through positive times.

The Rademacher, Alexandrov, Jensen and theorem-of-sums chain retains full AC. Half-relaxed contact recovery explicitly uses Countable Choice. Null sets in the differentiability chain use closed-cube-cover nullity.
Scheme extensions are multilinear in space and constant on time intervals; convergence is locally uniform through each T'<T. Semi-Lagrangian convergence additionally requires h_max²/τ→0.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every open U⊆R^n and locally Lipschitz map u:U→R^m, u is Frechet differentiable outside a null subset of U.

Under AC, for USC u_i on open Euclidean domains and a local maximum of Σ_i u_i(x_i)−φ(x) at z, with φ C² and A=D²φ(z), every ε>0 admits closed superjets (D_iφ(z),X_i) satisfying −(ε⁻¹+||A||)I≤diag(X_i)≤A+εA².

Under AC and the exact finite-control coefficient hypotheses of the diagonal-diffusion model, bounded USC subsolutions and bounded LSC supersolutions with pointwise ordered raw relaxed initial traces satisfy u≤v on the periodic interior cylinder.
Assume AC. A finite locally semiconvex function on an open subset of R^n, n≥1, has a direction-uniform second-order Peano expansion with symmetric quadratic matrix outside a cube-cover-null set.

Under AC, finite convex functions on open convex Euclidean sets have nonempty locally bounded subdifferentials with locally closed graph; singleton subdifferentials characterize differentiability. On every closed ball compactly inside the domain there is a globally Lipschitz convex extension H agreeing there. For F=H+|x|²/2, F* is finite C¹ and DF* is one-Lipschitz, with DF*(p)=x iff p∈∂F(x).

Strict smooth interior contacts of upper or lower half-relaxed limits of locally bounded periodic interpolant extensions localize to recovering nodal maxima or minima on a fixed closed space-time ball, along mesh indices tending to infinity; sequential recovery uses Countable Choice.
The periodic tensor interpolant has nonnegative weights summing to one, preserves order and bounds the sup norm; for periodic C² φ, ||I_hφ−φ||∞≤(1/8)Σ_j h_j²||∂_jjφ||∞.

For refining diagonal-diffusion schemes satisfying diffusion dominance and CFL at every row, the spatially multilinear, temporally constant extensions have bounded USC subsolution and bounded LSC supersolution half-relaxed limits with the prescribed relaxed initial traces; coincidence is not asserted.
For every policy π, A^π=cI−Q^π is nonsingular, its inverse is entrywise nonnegative, and each inverse diagonal entry is strictly positive.

For the declared first-order coefficients, refining periodic grids and time steps, and finite control sets with vanishing bounded-momentum Hamiltonian errors, the semi-Lagrangian scheme under h_max²/τ→0 and the upwind scheme under CFL converge locally uniformly on the periodic cylinder through T'<T to the same bounded continuous viscosity solution.

concerns.concern: The Statement describes V_k only as 'periodic interpolant extensions', while proof step 1.2 explicitly uses 'the piecewise-constant time extension' to recover a nearby grid-time value. Specify the temporal extension in the Statement, or state the temporal convex-combination property needed for recovery. Both actual scheme consumers already prescribe piecewise-constant time extensions, so their uses satisfy the proof's intended hypothesis.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier grid definition and complete convex-interpolation proof against the local unit-period specialization and interpolation lemma. Positive periods and N_j≥1 permit the local restriction to unit periods and N_j≥3. The supplier gives convexity and sup-norm contraction at every foot without a displacement restriction. The HJB Euler foot and consistency argument are local; no C¹ characteristic-flow theorem is imported for merely Lipschitz coefficients.

The actual item edge is lem-bem-lipschitz-graph-sobolev-and-green-interface → thm-na-rademacher-euclidean. Its F1 and steps 1.1/3.1 use almost-everywhere differentiability of Lipschitz graph functions and locally Lipschitz compositions under explicitly declared AC. These satisfy the supplier's hypotheses. Weak-derivative identification is separately attributed to the ACL characterization, rather than claimed as an additional conclusion of Rademacher.
